models.purpose: Minimize the time of the last person out.
models.summary: The building is a network of halls, intersections and stairs, with exits as terminal nodes. Escape time is split into four phases: room and channel, stairs, the exit, and a delay from falls and trampling. The objective minimizes the maximum over floors and routes of the sum of the four phase times. Each phase time is itself a maximum of distance over normal speed plus congested length over congested speed. An edge can carry at most its capacity times the phase time. Minimizing the room and exit phases reduces to shortening the congested length, which reduces to lowering the flow through the jammed node while keeping the floor total fixed. An improved Dijkstra drops stairs the evacuee cannot reach and stairs likely to jam before searching. Against a random assignment the model cuts time 39.3 percent, congestion 24 percent and injuries 60.69 percent, from 239 injured to 94.

models.purpose: Move people off a jammed node to a clearer one.
models.summary: On one floor, the crowd at a node is the sum of the route flows through it. A share is redirected to a clearer node only when the excess over capacity exceeds the walk to that node; the redirected count is set to zero if the test fails. Between floors the same test is scaled by the number of floors still to descend, and the objective minimizes the sum of stair times. For the vulnerable, the delay phase multiplies the headcount by a fall probability and a stampede probability. The elderly and children move at half speed, pregnant women and the disabled at a fifth; their shares are 11, 5, 1 and 2.5 percent. Normal speeds are 2 m/s in rooms and 0.25 m/s on stairs, falling to 0.5 and 0.0625 under congestion.

models.purpose: Stretch the phase times by a disaster grade and cap the entering staff.
models.summary: A disaster grade from I to V maps to a factor phi0 from 0 to 2.5, using a normal speed of 2 m/s and a maximum of 5. Each phase time is then multiplied by one plus the factor, and the fall and stampede terms grow by the same factor. Emergency staff may enter only through exits whose predicted finish is earlier than the latest, and only up to the spare capacity, so the last evacuee is not delayed. Any route whose evacuees would then finish after the latest is dropped and the next shortest is taken. For a fire in area 338, the pyramid admits 240 staff in 229 seconds and the Lions Gate 410 in 370 seconds; Richelieu and the Carrousel touch the longest route, so they admit none. Losing the pyramid exit delays evacuation 48.3 percent to 782 seconds; losing area 338 delays it 20 percent to 632.5 seconds.
